Apply

Description

The Retreat at Canton is seeking a FT Housekeeper to join their team!

Shift Details

Housekeeper

Tuesday-Saturday

The Housekeeper is responsible for performing all housekeeping activities such as, but not limited to, dusting, vacuuming, sweeping, mopping, laundry, shampooing carpets, scrubbing bathrooms, cleaning counters, taking out the trash and cleaning windows. Responsibilities also include restocking common area bistroâs and bathrooms, resident rooms and bathrooms with the appropriate paper products and hand soap.

Principle Duties And Responsibilities

Housekeeping

  • Follow detailed cleaning worksheet/ checklist for each room and common area
  • Responsible for the set-up and mixing of water and detergents, in proper containers to prepare cleaning solutions, according to specifications
  • Follow procedures for the use of chemical cleaners and power equipment, in order to prevent damage to floors and fixtures
  • Clean community common area and resident room(s) floors and walls by sweeping, mopping, scrubbing, and / or vacuuming
  • Steam clean or shampoo carpet
  • Dust furniture, walls, machines and equipment which include moving furniture around
  • Clean windows, glass partitions, and mirrors, using soapy water or other cleaner, sponges and squeegees
  • Make adjustments to heating cooling and ventilation system which may include changing filters
  • Gather and empty trash
  • Remove debris from outdoor porches, parking lot and dumpster area
  • Ensure all bathrooms (common area, resident) are stocked with toilet paper, paper towels, Kleenex and liquid and soap
  • Replace light bulbs throughout the community
  • Ensure all suites that have 2 residents residing are cleaned twice a week
  • Notify supervisor, by documenting in the maintenance log and housekeeping checklist, concerning the need for major repairs or additions to the building operating systems

#86pgm

Requirements

EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE/LICENSURE- CERTIFICATION

Housekeeper

  • Education: High School Diploma/ GED required
  • One (1) year job related experience

Skills And Abilities

  • Understanding of infection control procedures
  • Demonstrate the ability to Multi task and Manage Stress
  • Understands and embraces the assisted living philosophy
  • Ability to work weekends, evenings and flexible hours, available for our customers at peak service delivery days and times
  • Possess written and verbal skills for effective communication

Building a sustainable tomorrow

KierBAM are a Joint Venture (JV) partnership between Kier and BAM UK & Ireland - BAM UK & Ireland's infrastructure segment is currently delivering the redevelopment project at a Royal Navy site located in Plymouth and we are seeking an experienced Service Locator.


The Service Locator will carry out the physical check and survey of all of the underground services within the area that is being investigated, the Service Locator will have the following responsibilities. You will use various geophysical techniques to locate the service, once they have been found, the services will be marked/spray painted onto the ground in the appropriate colour, defining the type and depth of the service. You will also maintain the contents of the permits on site, making sure the workforce remains compliant with conditions and processes outlined within the permits.

Due to the site being a high-security military naval base, additional security checks will be required a BPSS level of security clearance is necessary. These checks can take up to 8 weeks to process. Only candidates holding EU, NATO, 5 Eyes, or MISWG member passports and who have been UK residents for the last 5 years can be considered for this role.

Your team
  • Location: Devonport Dockyard, Plymouth
  • Contract: Permanent, 42.5 hours a week
Making Possible

In this role as Service Locator, you will be working in a live MOD facility. Your day-to-day tasks will include:

  • Authorise Permit to Break Surface
  • Ensure compliance with and enforcement of the project permit for the Break Ground procedure
  • Review method statements tailored to specific tasks
  • Mark all services within the work boundaries to protect colour standards
  • Provide teams with an overview of the services within their designated work boundaries and discuss methods for working around those affected services.
  • Implement an 8-point checklist during work gang briefings
  • Enforce any designated exclusion zones surrounding affected services
  • Obtain the required signatures for permit approval from the works team and the Project Engineer
  • Notify the BOSC of any discrepancies in the records
  • Investigate uncharted services as directed by the BOSC
  • Inform the BOSC of any services that have been removed from the work area, ensuring the service drawings are updated accordingly
  • Attach the most current SMD CAD drawing to the permit-to-dig
  • Ensure that no work gang operates under an expired permit for breaking ground or in an area lacking a permit.
  • Maintain service markings for the duration of the permit as well as incremental scans as excavations progress
  • This profile is not exhaustive. From time to time, you may be required by the Company to perform other tasks, which are not included in the above description, but are within your capabilities and, where necessary, training, and full support will be given
What do you bring to the role?

Essential:

  • We are seeking a candidate who can handle multiple tasks, show flexibility, and become a key contributor to our team
  • A CSCS Card is required (this must be obtained before commencing work)
  • Familiarity with Electromagnetic location and ground penetrating radar is essential
  • A solid understanding of industry practices and standards related to utility detection, including PAS 128 and TSA, is important
  • Candidates should have a proficient working knowledge of surveying equipment, such as GPR, CAT, and Genny utility detection tools
  • The ability to collaborate and communicate effectively within a team and interact with clients on-site is required
  • Knowledge of HSG-47 and GS-6

Desirable

  • Experience in the Nuclear environment would be considered beneficial
  • QCF Level 3 or Level 5 certification in utility mapping is preferred
  • Applicants should possess a minimum of 2-3 years of utility surveying experience
Whats in it for you?
  • Competitive salary
  • A wide range of family-friendly policies
  • Company car/car allowance/travel allowance
  • 8 % matched pension contributions
  • Private healthcare
  • Life assurance
  • 26 days holiday
  • 2 wellbeing days
  • 1 volunteering day
  • Personal and professional development
About BAM

Building a sustainable tomorrow. Thats our mission and our promise at BAM. Its how we engineer vital infrastructure and construct high-quality buildings as one of the largest construction companies in Europe.

We strive to create an environment where everybody feels welcome and valued. Were on an exciting journey to employ the best talent to join us regardless of social background, race, colour, religion, national or ethnic origin, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability or other characteristics.

title: Chief Operating Officer
description: Description The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is the senior operational leader of U.S. Hunger, responsible for translating enterprise strategy into daily execution. This role owns P&L performance across all business lines â Full Cart, Hunger Projects, and the Data/Intelligence engine â ensuring the organization's earned-income model (97%+ of total revenue) operates with precision, accountability, and scalability. The COO must bring the instincts of an entrepreneur and the discipline of a corporate operator: connecting dots others miss, asking tough questions that drive clarity, and building the systems that allow talented leaders to perform at their highest level. Operational excellence and mission-aligned impact are not in tension here â they are the same thing. Enterprise Operations & P&L Execution Own P&L execution across all business lines â each engine must meet its margin, revenue, and impact targets. Establish and drive the operating cadence â monthly reviews, quarterly business performance reporting, and clear accountability across departments. Make resource allocation decisions across competing priorities â deploying people, capital, and attention against the highest-value opportunities. Present operational performance, capacity, and growth execution to the Board of Directors. Partner with the CEO on scenario planning, structural growth strategies, and enterprise-wide decision-making. Program Leadership â Full Cart & Hunger Projects Provide executive oversight of Full Cart and Hunger Projects â ensuring delivery excellence, measurable outcomes, and scalability. Partner with program directors to evaluate, evolve, and scale programs in response to partner needs, market opportunities, and operational realities. Drive integration between program design, data infrastructure, and client-facing delivery â ensuring mission impact and revenue execution are operationally connected. Oversee supply chain and logistics operations to ensure consistent, high-quality program delivery at scale. Revenue Growth & Partner Execution Own enterprise revenue execution across health plan partnerships, corporate engagement, and strategic growth opportunities â ensuring acquisition and retention targets are consistently met. Drive strategies that deepen existing partner relationships and expand engagement across multiple service lines, maximizing long-term value and organizational sustainability. Represent U.S. Hunger externally with payors, partners, and stakeholders â translating operational insight into compelling value propositions that differentiate USH in the market. Leverage buyer-side CSR experience and existing relationships across the corporate social impact and food access ecosystem to accelerate partner acquisition and deepen engagement. Cross-Functional Alignment & Executive Leadership Partner with the Chief Technology Officer to define business requirements, program design priorities, and operational needs that shape the technology and data roadmap â ensuring platform delivery enables execution across all business lines. Manage the VP of Finance & Enterprise KPIs and VP of People & Culture â two executives who maintain direct visibility to the CEO through their seat at the executive table â ensuring fiscal discipline, enterprise analytics, and workforce strategy are aligned with operational goals. Actively contribute to organizational governance, strategy, and enterprise-wide decision-making as the CEO's primary operational counterpart. Team Leadership & Development Build, lead, and develop a high-performing operational leadership team â setting clear expectations, driving accountability, and coaching leaders who are growing into executive-level roles. Develop performance metrics and accountability systems that connect individual and team outcomes to enterprise financial and impact objectives. Promote a culture of rigorous inquiry, collaboration, and continuous improvement â where leaders are expected to think critically, challenge assumptions, and own their outcomes. Foster an environment where staff understand both the business drivers of USH's earned-income model and the transformative impact of their work on the communities served. These essential job functions are not to be construed as a complete statement of all duties performed. Employees will be required to perform other duties as required. Requirements 10+ years of progressive leadership in operations, business management, or revenue execution â with direct P&L ownership. Experience building, running, or scaling a business â including sales growth, client retention, and financial performance accountability. Proven ability to lead and develop directors and VPs â coaching strong operators into executive-level leaders while holding them accountable to outcomes. Demonstrated pattern of connecting dots across functions â seeing how operational, financial, people, and program decisions impact each other. Experience at the board level â presenting performance, defending strategy, and engaging C-suite stakeholders directly. Experience in mission-driven, earned-income environments where market discipline and social impact must coexist. About SuperPlane

SuperPlane is an open source software factory engine: the system that lets AI agents build, test, and ship code while engineers focus on design and decisions. This is going to be how all software gets built, and we're building the engine underneath it.

The Role

We are hiring a product engineer to join the team and own meaningful projects end to end.

This is a remote role. We currently work across GMT+2 to GMT-3 and welcome candidates in that range.

At SuperPlane, we don't split engineering into frontend and backend. Everyone is a well-rounded builder who moves across the stack, makes product and technical calls, asks for help when needed, and delivers features from start to finish. You might spend one day building an API endpoint or workflow engine improvement, and the next day polishing a React surface that users touch every day.

We're looking for someone at a mid-level to senior level: you've shipped real products, you can work independently, and you're ready to grow fast in a high-trust, high-pace environment. You don't need to have done everything before, but you need to learn quickly and take ownership of what you build.


What We Are Looking For

  • You are genuinely full-stack.

  • Your workflow is AI-driven and you know how to stay fast without getting sloppy.

  • You have strong backend experience in a systems-oriented language. While we use Go, we don't expect you to be an expert already, just to ramp up fast.

  • You have solid systems judgment. APIs, data models, reliability, and trade-offs matter to you.

  • You're comfortable with TypeScript and React -- the modern frontend stack.

  • You are comfortable with cloud-native tooling and modern software delivery.

  • You want ownership, not a narrow lane.

  • You want an early-stage company where the pace is high, the standards are high, and the upside is big.


How To Apply

We care more about proof of work than polished applications, and we want to see how you show up in open source.

Before you apply, submit at least one pull request to superplanehq/superplane. It can be small and it does not need to be merged.

When you apply, send your GitHub username and a link to your pull request. We verify both, and applications missing either field will not move forward.


Why You'll Love Working at SuperPlane

  • Build a frontier product used by engineers across the globe.

  • Meaningful equity and real ownership.

  • Small team, fast feedback loops.

  • Remote role that lets you focus and create.

description: If you enjoy hands-on work, learning advanced restoration techniques, and mentoring others, this is the role for you. As a Contents Crew Lead (Internally known as Contents Technician II), you'll play a key part in helping people recover what matters most. You'll take pride in restoring items affected by fire, water, and mold while guiding teammates, mastering specialized equipment, and making a real impact on every project. A DAY IN THE LIFE OF A CONTENTS CREW LEAD As a Contents Crew Lead, no two days are ever the same. One morning you might be restoring treasured family photos, and by afternoon you could be cleaning specialized equipment or mentoring a new team member. You roll up your sleeves and dive into each job with focus and pride, using advanced tools and cleaning systems to bring belongings back to life. You track and photograph contents, keep meticulous records, and make sure every item is handled with care. You troubleshoot, problem-solve, and stay one step ahead to keep projects on schedule. You take ownership of your work and lead by example, creating a positive, efficient, and safe environment for your team. Every day, your skill, energy, and attention to detail help turn chaos into calm for clients when they need it most. You'll help communities rebuild and families recover after unexpected events. We offer competitive pay, comprehensive health and dental benefits, and RRSP matching because we believe in taking care of our people. You'll have opportunities to learn, grow, and build a lasting career across Canada in a culture that values care, collaboration, and doing the right thing. If you enjoy hands-on work, learning advanced restoration techniques, and mentoring others, this is the role for you. As a Contents Crew Lead (Internally known as Contents Technician II), you'll play a key part in helping people recover what matters most. You'll take pride in restoring items affected by fire, water, and mold while guiding teammates, mastering specialized equipment, and making a real impact on every project.

A DAY IN THE LIFE OF A CONTENTS CREW LEAD

As a Contents Crew Lead, no two days are ever the same. One morning you might be restoring treasured family photos, and by afternoon you could be cleaning specialized equipment or mentoring a new team member. You roll up your sleeves and dive into each job with focus and pride, using advanced tools and cleaning systems to bring belongings back to life. You track and photograph contents, keep meticulous records, and make sure every item is handled with care. You troubleshoot, problem-solve, and stay one step ahead to keep projects on schedule. You take ownership of your work and lead by example, creating a positive, efficient, and safe environment for your team. Every day, your skill, energy, and attention to detail help turn chaos into calm for clients when they need it most.

Qualifications

  • Minimum 1 year of experience in restoration, emergency services, or a related field
  • Strong knowledge of cleaning methods for fire, water, and mold restoration
  • Experience operating Ozone and Hydroxyl machines or similar restoration equipment
  • Excellent attention to detail with strong organizational and teamwork skills
  • Ability to guide and support Contents Technician I team members
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite and comfortable using mobile devices and apps
  • Certifications required: Water Damage Restoration Technician (WRT), Fire and Smoke Restoration Technician (FSRT), and Odor Control Technician (OCT)
  • Additional certifications considered an asset: Commercial Carpet Cleaning (CCT), Carpet Repair and Reinstallation (RRT), Upholstery and Fabric Cleaning (UFT), and Applied Microbial Remediation (AMRT)
  • Valid driver's license and clean driving abstract
  • Must be able to participate in a rotating on-call scheduleâ¯â¯â¯
  • Ability to complete work activities which may include physical labour, material handling and lifting, climbing ladders, wearing a respirator, and working in tight spaces (attics, basements, and crawlspaces)

About Viva Wellness Drip

Viva Wellness Drip is a rapidly growing concierge wellness company dedicated to delivering premium healthcare experiences directly to our clients. We specialize in mobile IV therapy, wellness injections, peptide programs, aesthetic treatments, concierge nursing, corporate wellness services, luxury hospitality partnerships, and wellness activations throughout the United States.

This is not a traditional Executive Assistant position.

We're looking for someone who enjoys bringing structure to a fast-moving business, solving problems before they arise, keeping projects organized, and ensuring nothing falls through the cracks.


As our Executive Operations & Project Manager, you'll serve as the operational right hand to our founders, helping coordinate priorities, manage projects, improve communication across departments, and keep multiple business initiatives moving forward simultaneously.


Every day will look different. One day you may be coordinating a new service launch, the next you may be helping onboard new contractors, organizing company documentation, following up on strategic partnerships, or helping prepare for a major corporate wellness event.


If you're someone who thrives in an entrepreneurial environment, enjoys wearing multiple hats, and wants to grow alongside a rapidly expanding company, we'd love to hear from you.

Executive Operations

  • Coordinate executive travel and logistics when needed.
  • Assist with executive correspondence and internal communications.


Project Management

  • Keep company projects organized and moving forward.
  • Coordinate timelines across multiple departments.
  • Follow up with vendors, contractors, partners, and internal team members.
  • Assist with launching new services, programs, and business initiatives.
  • Help identify operational bottlenecks and recommend solutions.

Business Operations

  • Organize company files, documents, and internal systems.
  • Maintain and update Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
  • Assist with contractor onboarding and administrative processes.
  • Help improve operational workflows and efficiencies.
  • Coordinate communication between departments.
  • Support day-to-day administrative and operational needs.


Cross-Functional Support

Work closely with our founders and collaborate with departments including:

  • Business Development
  • Marketing
  • Operations
  • Clinical Services
  • Dispatch & Wellness Coordinators
  • Inventory Management
  • Events & Corporate Wellness

You'll help ensure projects remain aligned, organized, and progressing efficiently across the organization.


Qualifications:


Required

  • Minimum 3 years of experience supporting executives, founders, or leadership teams.
  • Strong project management and organizational skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication.
  • Exceptional attention to detail.
  • Ability to prioritize multiple projects simultaneously.
  • High level of professionalism and discretion when handling confidential information.
  • Proficiency with Google Workspace and Microsoft Office.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Must be located within commuting distance of Los Angeles, California.


Preferred

  • Experience working in a startup or high-growth company.
  • Healthcare, wellness, hospitality, or concierge service experience.
  • Experience creating or improving business systems and operational processes.
  • Familiarity with project management platforms such as Asana, ClickUp, Monday.com, Trello, or Notion.
  • Experience supporting multiple executives or departments.


What We're Looking For

The ideal candidate is proactive, dependable, resourceful, and naturally takes ownership.

You're the type of person who notices problems before others do, enjoys creating organization from complexity, communicates professionally, and takes pride in helping a business operate more efficiently.


You don't wait to be told what to doâyou anticipate needs, solve problems, and help move the company forward.


Most importantly, you're excited about joining a fast-growing company where you'll have the opportunity to grow your responsibilities and make a meaningful impact.


Compensation & Growth

This position begins as a 1099 Independent Contractor through an initial 90-day contract-to-hire engagement.


The first 90 days are intended to ensure a strong mutual fit while providing an opportunity for both you and Viva Wellness Drip to build a successful long-term working relationship.


Following a successful engagement, there is significant opportunity for increased hours, expanded responsibilities, and transition into a long-term part-time or full-time role as the company continues to grow.


Why Join Viva Wellness Drip?

At Viva Wellness Drip, you'll work directly alongside the founders of an ambitious and rapidly expanding concierge wellness company.


Your work will have a direct impact on how the company grows, scales, and operates. You'll help build systems, improve efficiency, support exciting new initiatives, and contribute to a company that's redefining how wellness services are delivered.

  • If you're looking for a role where your ideas matter, your work has a meaningful impact, and your career can grow alongside an innovative company, we'd love to hear from you.

title: A Book of Your Own
description: Editorâs Note: The following piece, by the late, great Herman Holtz, was to appear as part of Hermanâs âHindsights & Insightsâ column. It is part of our collection of âclassicsââarticles that stand the test of time no matter how many technologies come and go. Published with permission. It seems, from what I read every day on the TECHWR-L list, that it isnât at all easy for most people to break into a beginning tech writing job. Of course, that kind of Catch 22âyou need a job to get the experience you need to qualify for the jobâis far from unknown, especially in the high-tech working world. Itâs why prospective employers want to see clips and other evidence that you can write reasonably well, whether it is technical or not, before they will consider you. I was a tech writer long before I wrote my first book, although I had to jump through some difficult hoops to land my first tech writing job (a series of six tests on technology); however, a great deal of my work later, especially my consulting jobs, came about as a result of my books and the reputation they bestowed on me. Being published between covers brings you respect almost as quickly and surely as becoming known as a millionaire business owner does. Even now, it happens. A reader who owns a small business in Baltimore hired me recently to do some consulting with him, after reading one of my books published a few years ago. The gentleman had read several books on the subject of proposal writing and contracting, and he decided that my book reflected the kind of thinking he needed, although it was one of my most slender volumes. It is really not that difficult to turn out your first book if you select a subject that you are reasonably familiar with (and so can research efficiently) and plan ahead with a solid and well-thought-out outline. Remember that what you write does not have to be a thick tome. My books have generally run to about 275 to 500 pages, but I have also written my share of books that printed out to fewer than 200 pages. There Are Many Ways To Get Ideas For Books, And The More You Concentrate On The Need, The More New Ideas You Will Get. Here Are Just a Few Tips Start reading the periodicals that deal with the subject Probably they will be trade journals and may touch only lightly on the subject, but that is fine. But, how much is there to say about the subject? Is it useful detailâthat is, does a lightly-covered detail justify a book of its own? The book of mine I referred to here is a small book that presents sharply-focused abstracts on what I think to be the most important topics about proposal writingâa subject on which I have written more than one large, detailed book. The little book referred to here is virtually the opposite of expanding an article or two into a book. Browse libraries and book stores for current books on the subject Would you go about writing a book on the subject entirely differently? Would it be a better book? How? Why? Read books that devote a chapter to the subject. How about developing that chapter into a full book of its own? Think about what that information might mean to readers and to which readers Will it help someone start or improve their business? Improve their position in some way? Make it easier to learn a given subject? Think about the need for the information Is the subject a very popular one? Is it on how to be a better golfer, for example? Hard to lose with any good book on golf. The same for many other subjects. There is never an end to new books about the Civil War, even if you call it The War Between the States. But if you want your first book (I hope that it will be only your first) to help your business career, it is best to choose a serious business subject or other how-to book. Finally, remember that you donât have to write the book in a day. Do a few pages each day, and you will be surprised at how soon you have a book. title: This IS Your Dream Job
description: Here are two questions to ask yourself: 1) when are you most content? (Not âhappyâ per se, since happy moments are fleeting. 2) Does contentment ever happen for you during the workday? The average American worker spends 2080 hours per year on paid work. title: Ship to Shore Technician
description: Job Description As a Ship-to-Shore Technician, you will play a vital role in supporting the safe and efficient operation of vessels arriving and departing at the port. This position involves working on the dock to ensure the proper mooring, securing, and release of ships, while maintaining safety and operational standards. In addition to mooring responsibilities, the role will also involve performing general maintenance and support tasks as required to ensure overall port and equipment readiness. The Ship-to-Shore Technician is responsible for, but not limited to the following: Docking and Undocking Operations Assist in safely docking and undocking cruise ships at port using mooring lines, ropes, and related equipment. Work in coordination with the shipâs captain, crew, and port authorities to ensure that vessels are safely secured and aligned with docking infrastructure. Mooring Line Management: Handle and manage mooring lines, ensuring they are properly fastened, tense, and released. Perform visual inspection of mooring lines and related equipment regularly for wear and damage, ensuring everything is in safe working condition. (Regularly performed by ship crew) Ship and Dock Safety Maintain safety protocols during mooring procedures, ensuring that all tasks are performed in accordance with safety regulations. Monitor weather conditions and report any changes that could affect docking or undocking procedures. Communication and Coordination Communicate effectively with other team members on board and shore-based personnel. Work with the Port Authorities to ensure the timely and safe transfer of passengers and cargo. Emergency Procedures Be trained to respond in case of an emergency during docking or undocking operations, including accidents or hazardous situations. Ensure all mooring operations are conducted efficiently and safely, even under adverse weather conditions or emergencies. PPE Equipment (MANDATORY) Must always be in possession of steel toe boots (or prescribed non-slip safety shoes), safety vest, hard hat, gloves, radio/communication device. (To be provided by Carnival) Cleaning & Maintenance of Pier & Mooring Equipment & Fixtures: Ensure all mooring equipment such as winches, ropes, and fenders are properly maintained and operational (through visual checks and inspections). Gangway Inspections & Maintenance: Inspect gangway components for wear, corrosion, proper tension, secure connections, and smooth operation to ensure safe pedestrian access and functionality. Fenders: Conduct visual inspections of pier fenders and associated hardware to identify cracks, deformation, excessive wear, or damage caused by vessel contact, and report deficiencies as needed. Mooring Bollards: Regularly inspect mooring bollards for structural integrity, including corrosion, cracks, loose anchor bolts, foundation stress, and coating condition, to ensure safe vessel mooring. Stanchions & Pier Fixtures: Inspect stanchions and associated components for corrosion, damage, misalignment, or instability, ensuring they remain secure and serviceable. Ropes: Inspect ropes for wear, fraying, or damage, and verify they are properly positioned and suitable for continued use. Mooring Equipment Maintenance: Perform minor maintenance and repairs of mooring equipment when necessary. Pier & Dock Cleaning: Maintain clean, safe, and non-slip pier surfaces by removing dirt, salt, algae, stains, debris and other buildup by pressure washing and using prescribed cleaning equipment and solutions, along all designated cruise pier and trestle areas. Cleaning Equipment Operation: Safely inspect, operate, and maintain cleaning equipment, including scrubbers and pressure washers, ensuring proper use, cleaning, and storage after each operation. Additional Maintenance Support Activities Perform minor maintenance support to technical teams including plumbing, electrical, masonry, carpentry, and HVAC functions. Mandatory Training: Maintain compliance with organizational requirements by attending and participating in all required company training sessions. Lagoon Care Perform maintenance/inspections of lagoon systems. Education: Education: High School Diploma. Maintenance knowledge is preferred. Certified Pool Operator (CPO) required within 6 months of employment start. Three to Five years' experience working in a mooring or associated fields. Essential Experience Required: Must be physically fit. Must have strong customer service skills. Ability to work in an outdoor environment. Ability to multi-task and think critically. Previous work experience preferred. Prolonged periods standing and working outside. Must be able to lift, up to 50 pounds at times. All island employees must be physically able to participate in emergency lifesaving procedures and drills. Full use/range of motion of arms and legs as well as full visual, verbal and hearing abilities are required to receive and give instructions in the event of an emergency. Ability to read and write English to understand and interpret written procedures. This includes the ability to give and receive instructions in written and verbal forms and to effectively present information and respond to questions from guests, managers, and co-workers. title: Program & Events Coordinator
description: About the LSPA: The LSP Association (LSPA) is a non-profit association for Massachusetts Licensed Site Professionals (LSPs) and other related environmental practitioners who work on behalf of property owners, operators, and other involved parties to assess and cleanup oil and hazardous materials (OHM) released to the environment. LSPs are licensed by the Commonwealth to oversee this work and, since 1993, over 40,000 contaminated properties have been brought into regulatory compliance. The LSPA's mission is to support our membership in achieving and maintaining a high standard of practice in the assessment and remediation of contaminated sites in Massachusetts and New England. The LSPA provides technical and educational resources to our membership in the form of programming, networking events, committees, and resources. The LSPA also serves as an advocate to the profession with MassDEP, the LSP Board of Registration, and the state legislature, and as a resource to the public. Job Description: The Program & Events Coordinator plays a critical role in the success of the LSPA and serves as a primary point of contact for our members, volunteers, and sponsors. This individual is responsible for planning, coordinating, and executing the association's educational programs and networking events, administering the sponsorship program, and providing customer service support. Success in this position means delivering high-quality member experiences, maintaining strong relationships with volunteers and sponsors, and ensuring the smooth administration of our continuing education program. The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, customer-focused, and comfortable managing multiple projects simultaneously. This individual enjoys working independently while collaborating closely with volunteers, board members, speakers, sponsors, and staff. Key Responsibilities: Educational Programs : Coordinate, plan, and manage programs and speakers for all LSPA courses, membership meetings, emerging professional events, the Annual Fall Party, and the Environmental Symposium. The LSPA hosts one to three events per month with 25-250 people in attendance. Approximately 65% of programming is hosted virtually. Content creation is performed in conjunction with input from the Executive Director, Committee Chairs, Education Committee, and Board of Directors. Event Logistics: For in-person events, source event venues and help facilitate contracts; plan food and beverage, room set-up, and audiovisual needs; reconcile venue bills; and serve as the point of contact on-site. For virtual programs, setup and run the virtual meeting platform, monitor attendance and engagement, create moderator scripts and slides, and train speakers on how to use the virtual platform. Continuing Education (CE) Administration : Compile CE materials for all educational courses and meetings; submit materials for credit approval with the LSP Board of Registration, the Connecticut Licensed Environmental Professional (LEP) Board, and other Boards/entities; maintain CE records related to attendance, engagement, and evaluation; issue certificates of attendance to attendees; and attend monthly virtual LSP Board of Registration meetings. Sponsorship : Help administer the corporate and event sponsorship program, including updating the sponsorship prospectus, facilitating invoices/payments, maintaining contact lists, conducting outreach, and working with sponsors to access their sponsorship benefits. Member Service and Organizational Support : Help monitor and respond to inquiries received through the organization email inbox; provide customer service to members, sponsors, speakers, and event attendees; attend Board meetings, leadership meetings, and committee meetings as requested; and support association operations and special projects as needed. Qualifications The person hired for this role should have the following qualifications: Experience: 2-5 years of experience in program/event planning, project management, or another related field. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, and proven ability to provide excellent customer service. Strong project management skills with excellent attention to detail. Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines independently. Comfortable coordinating, building relationships with, and communicating professionally with members, volunteers, sponsors, vendors, and other external stakeholders/partners. Technology: Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, Word, Excel, PowerPoint). Zoom Meetings and Zoom Webinar, including coordinating presenters from multiple locations, incorporating polling, and managing technical issues. Association management systems (AMS) or member databases. Online registration and evaluation platforms. Canva or similar design tools (preferred, not required). Preferred Qualifications (not required): Experience working for a nonprofit organization, professional association, or membership-based organization. Experience with the environmental sciences industry. Familiarity with sponsorship development or relationship management. Bachelor's degree, Associate's degree with relevant experience, or significant relevant professional experience demonstrating the knowledge, skills, and abilities required to perform the position successfully. Why Join the LSPA? This is an opportunity to work with a respected association that supports environmental professionals making a meaningful impact on public health and environmental protection throughout Massachusetts and New England. As a small organization, we offer autonomy, flexibility, and the opportunity to build relationships with industry leaders while helping shape the educational and professional development experiences of our members. Compensation and benefits include: Salary : The salary range for this position is $70,000â$80,000 annually. Compensation will be based on a variety of factors such as individual qualifications and experience. Benefits : LSPA employees receive $300 per month for a Healthcare Reimbursement Account (HRA) that may be used to reimburse certain medical and insurance-related expenses. The organization does not currently offer group health or dental insurance plans. In addition, employees have access to a 401(k) plan. PTO : 15 days of paid time off (PTO) annually for the first three years (increases to 20 days thereafter). The LSPA also provides 14 holidays per year (inclusive of 5 floating holidays). Fully remote position : Candidates may reside anywhere in New England, with preference given to Massachusetts-based applicants. Travel to Massachusetts-based programs and events approximately 10â12 times annually is required. Reimbursement for home office expenses : $750 annually. How to Apply Please submit a cover letter and resume to mmorris@lspa.org. Applications without cover letters or that request compensation/benefits beyond what we can provide will not be reviewed. The LSPA is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, contact mmorris@lspa.org. The LSPA is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All employment decisions are based on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran, or disability status. Company: Ocean Hotels Barbados

SUMMARY: Performs a combination of tasks to maintain a high standard of cleanliness and orderliness in the hotel. To ensure guest rooms, working areas and the hotelâs premises in general in a clean and orderly manner.

Duties And Responsibilities

  • Operates in full compliance with the AAA 5 Diamond standards.
  • Cleans and sanitized rugs, carpets, and upholstered furniture - using vacuum cleaner, broom, as necessary.
  • Washes walls, ceilings, steps, patios, walkways, doors and window screens of the hotel rooms and public areas. Moves and arranges furniture, turns mattresses, hangs or removes fixtures, ornaments or pictures in guest rooms and offices as required.
  • Sweeps, mops, scrubs, sanitized, waxes, and polishes floors and immediate surroundings including lounge cushions.
  • Sweeps and scrubs corridors in front of guest rooms, removing any bottles.
  • Assists the Room Attendants in labour intensive tasks such as, flipping mattresses, hanging pictures and moving furniture or debris.
  • Make sure that outside areas such as patios and corridors are kept clean, sanitized, tidy and in working order.
  • Dusts and polishes metal work with Quimplex, (where applicable).
  • Collects soiled laundry for laundering, count dirty linen for collection, (where applicable).
  • Stores linen/literature supplies in service area closets.
  • Deliver clean linen or requested items to Room Attendants, (where applicable).
  • Clean, sanitized and polish elevator as often as possible
  • Assists with fixing of drapes etc.
  • Clean and sanitized linen chute, (where applicable).
  • Perform the specified duties at any of the properties of the Ocean Hotels Group.
  • Assist in any area that falls within your division. Perform any ancillary and / or related duties as may be assigned by Management.
  • Clean and sanitized gym daily including equipment; remove dirty towels and garbage, replenish water and clean towels, (where applicable).
  • Cleans ceiling fans, mirrors and glass doors, shower doors, lighting fixtures in rooms and public areas.
  • Cleans all directional signs, linen closet, electrical and exit doors of all corridors.
  • Attends daily briefings, departmental or other meetings as required.
  • Adheres to Company policies, standards and procedures, including Health and Safety, Fire Prevention, Hygiene and Discipline.
  • Attends training courses as agreed with Management, Human Resources Department or your Supervisor.
  • Assists in the lifting of heavy items in excess of 30lbs.
  • In addition to the duties which this job normally entails, you will be required to be completely flexible in this position and must be prepared to undertake such other work as may be assigned to you by the Company from time to time. Such work can be done outside the area of your normal duties.

Knowledge, Skills And Personal Attributes

Knowledge

The Houseman must have proficient knowledge in the following areas:

  • Understand, speak, read and write English at CXC level or equivalent
  • Level 2 or above National Vocational Qualification in Housekeeping

Skills

The Houseman must demonstrate the following skills:

  • Attention to detail and high level of accuracy
  • Time management skills
  • Read and write English fluently
  • Must be able to stand for extended periods of time
  • Must be neat, professional and well groomed
  • Must be able to lift up to 20 pounds (lifting above the shoulder is also required)
  • Ability to relate well to hotel guests and employees
  • Ability to understand and carry out oral and written instructions and request clarification when needed
  • A positive attitude and outgoing personality are essential
  • Must be able to work shifts (days, evenings, weekends, holidays and overtime)

Personal Attributes

The Houseman must demonstrate the following personal attributes

  • Hospitality
  • Creativity
  • Reliability
  • Compatibility
  • Effective follow up
  • Flexibility
  • Consistency
  • Professional deportment
